title: orobanche minor var. pubescens
intro: Orobanche minor var. pubescens, commonly known as the hairy broomrape, is a parasitic plant that belongs to the Orobanchaceae family. The hairy broomrape has been used in traditional medicine for its various health benefits, including anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial, and antioxidant properties, which can help to treat conditions such as fever, wounds, and digestive issues. The therapeutic actions of Orobanche minor var. pubescens include its ability to act as a diuretic, anti-spasmodic, and anti-diarrheal, making it a potential treatment for urinary problems, muscle spasms, and gastrointestinal disorders. The bioactive constituents of this plant include alkaloids, flavonoids, and phenolic acids, which contribute to its medicinal properties.
